newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end little changed in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end little changed in quiet market.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended the session little changed in very quiet trade on Monday, with the Memorial Day closing of the U.S. market sidelining many investors, analysts said.
"There's no indicators. There's no business. It's very, very quiet. There's nothing much interesting to say," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.05 to C$111.15 to yield 7.058 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond last traded with a yield of 6.99 percent on Friday. The spread between the bonds was unchanged at seven basis points.
"There was nothing going on at all," said Joe Lee, a portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management. "It's not unusual for the market to be flat on a day like this."
While there was no official close announced for the Canadian bond market, dealers said activity was extremely thin with the U.S. market closed for Memorial Day and London observing a banking holiday.
Trading volumes were also low because several brokerages were sponsoring golf tournaments on Monday, keeping many traders from the market.

Looking ahead, dealers said the focus for the week was likely to be new supply in Canada and the United States. Canada has a five-year bond auction on Wednesday, while the United States has a two-year note auction on Wednesday and a five-year note auction on Thursday.
Lee said the market could also see some new issues of corporate bonds.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.02 to C$103.32 to yield 6.524 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond last traded with a yield of 6.75 percent at the close of trading on Friday.
The negative spread between the two bonds was 23 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.88 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.15 percent.
